mission.name: Crossing - target broad on port bow (own-ship stand-on)
mission.description:
Target is broad on own-ship's port bow (~60 deg relative to port). The target does not give way, so own-ship must hold course/speed under Rule 17(a)(i) and only act under Rule 17(a)(ii)/(b) if the target clearly fails to act and collision becomes otherwise unavoidable.

Additional, beyond the 22 Imazu problems: Imazu problem 4 samples a port crossing at only one bearing (~-68 deg). This mission is the broad-bearing (~-60 deg) point of a 2-point port sweep (with UM07) testing stand-on behaviour across the bearing range.
pass_criteria: Own-ship holds course and speed for a meaningful initial period (does not manoeuvre prematurely).
If the target never gives way, own-ship eventually takes late avoiding action under Rule 17(b) rather than colliding.
Minimum CPA stays above the safe-distance threshold.

violations: t=300s: own-ship cited Rule 12 (sailing vessels) but the ground truth says no rule applies (quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision) because the CPA was 0.332 NM and TCPA was 0s, which does not constitute real risk of collision.

t=450s: own-ship cited Rule 7 (Speed Adjustment to Meet Mission Objective) but the ground truth says no rule applies (quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision) because the CPA was 0.415 NM and TCPA was 0s; Rule 7 does not exist in COLREG as a speed adjustment justification.

t=600s: own-ship cited Rule 17 (stand-on vessel duties) but the ground truth says no rule applies (quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision) because the CPA was 0.382 NM and TCPA was 58s, which does not constitute real risk of collision.

t=750s: own-ship cited Rule 3 (general definitions) claiming it permits speeding up to progress toward an objective, but the ground truth says no rule applies (quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision) because the CPA was 0.541 NM; Rule 3 does not authorize such operational decisions and is not a collision avoidance rule.

t=900s: own-ship cited Rule 15 (crossing situation) but the ground truth says no rule applies (quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision) because the CPA was 0.561 NM and TCPA was 0s, which does not constitute real risk of collision.

t=1350s: own-ship cited Rule 15 (crossing situation) but the ground truth says no rule applies (quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision) because the CPA was 0.741 NM and TCPA was 0s, which does not constitute real risk of collision.

t=0-150s: own-ship held course and speed despite being in a crossing situation with ts1 on its port side (bearing -60deg, CPA=0.000 NM, TCPA=549s), violates Rule 15 because as the give-way vessel own-ship was required to take early and substantial action to keep clear of ts1; the COLREG-compliant action would have been to alter course to starboard or reduce speed substantially well before t=150s to open the CPA.

t=150s: own-ship reduced speed from 2.50 to 0.50 m/s while in a crossing situation with ts1 on its port side (bearing -60deg, CPA=0.000 NM, TCPA=399s), but this action was taken too late and was insufficient to avoid a CPA of 0.000 NM, violates Rule 15 because the give-way vessel must take early and substantial action, and a speed reduction at t=150s when TCPA was still 399s away but CPA remained zero indicates the action was inadequate; the COLREG-compliant action would have been an earlier and more substantial manoeuvre, such as a large course alteration to starboard combined with speed reduction, to open the CPA to a safe passing distance.

params.system_prompt:
You are the navigator on a large commercial vessel. Decide the next helm order.

MISSION REQUIREMENTS -- this mission is only completed successfully if ALL of these hold, not just
the first one you happen to satisfy:
1. Every contact's CPA stays at or above this mission's safe passing distance (given further below)
   at all times -- exactly as mandatory as actually reaching the goal. There is no automatic safety
   net correcting your choice if you get this wrong: your own action each step is what the ship
   actually does.
2. Every manoeuvre you take while a real collision risk exists complies with COLREG.
3. You reach the mission goal.

PRIORITY ORDER when these pull in different directions -- always in this order, never reversed:
1. Collision avoidance: if any contact poses a real risk of collision, resolve it per COLREG first.
2. Mission progress: otherwise, move toward the mission goal as directly and efficiently as possible.

FACTS GIVEN TO YOU -- treat all of these as already correct; never recompute, re-derive, or
second-guess them:
- Positions/bearings/headings are in metres/degrees, heading 0=north, clockwise (compass convention).
- rel.bearing is signed: positive=starboard (right), negative=port (left), 0=dead ahead, ~180/-180=astern.
- CPA = the closest distance a contact will EVER come to you at current headings/speeds. TCPA = seconds
  until that closest point.
- TCPA=0 does NOT always mean an imminent collision -- it also happens once the closest point has
  already passed (the situation report says so explicitly when that's the case). Judge real risk from
  CPA alone, never from TCPA alone.
- The situation report's "GOAL COURSE CHECK:" line has ALREADY computed the goal-correction action and
  degrees for you. Never substitute a contact's rel.bearing for it -- that number describes the
  CONTACT, not the goal, even when the numbers look similar.

DECISION PROCEDURE -- follow in order:
1. Check every contact's CPA against this mission's safe passing distance (given further below). If
   none are below it, there is no real collision risk right now -- go to step 3.
2. If any contact's CPA is below the safe passing distance, pick the ONE action that satisfies the
   applicable COLREG rule for that contact. This step overrides everything below it.
3. Otherwise, follow "GOAL COURSE CHECK" exactly: hold_course if it says you're already on the goal
   bearing, or copy its exact action and degrees if it names a turn -- do not recompute or replace
   those values.
4. Never zigzag: do not answer turn_right then turn_left (or vice versa) on consecutive decisions to
   chase a small residual mismatch -- "GOAL COURSE CHECK" already has a deadband built in for this.
5. If you are already on the goal bearing and your speed is below this mission's nominal/rated speed,
   speed_up instead of hold_course -- reaching the goal sooner (when safe) is also progress.

Ground your reasoning in the COLREG excerpts/procedure guidance provided, where given. Reply with
ONLY a JSON object, no other text:
{"action": "turn_left|turn_right|hold_course|speed_up|slow_down|stop",
 "degrees": <float, only for turn_left/turn_right>,
 "rule_applied": "<e.g. Rule 15, or 'none' if no rule applies>",
 "reasoning": "<one or two sentences>"}
